year.shelter: Doesn't build anything. Lies down for the night under dense young spruces, out of the wind; in deep snow it stays in a small area with good food.
year.young: One or two calves (twins are common) born in May–June, hidden in thick cover. They follow their mother for a year.

food.spring: Fresh birch, willow and aspen shoots and leaves.
food.summer: Leaves of birch, willow, aspen and rowan, herbs, and water plants it wades in for.
food.autumn: Leaves while they last, bilberry shrubs, then twigs.
food.winter: Pine and birch twigs and shoots, and bark; it can eat over 10 kg a day.

year.notes: Bulls grow new antlers every spring and drop them in midwinter (December–February); in the game they follow the season (seasonal_parts). The autumn rut (September–October), when bulls call and spar, would be a great thing to show. Moose swim well.

text.title: Moose
text.menu_sub: Browse the treetops, wade into lakes, rest under the spruces.
text.menu_wild: Nothing here can hunt a grown moose.
text.intro_safe: Safe mode: explore! You're the biggest animal in the forest. Find young birches to eat.
text.intro_survival: Eat leaves and twigs to stay fed. At night, lie down under a spruce.
text.intro_wild: You're the king of the forest. Keep fed and rest under the spruces at night.
text.night_hint: It's night. Lie down under a big spruce's branches to sleep.
text.too_exposed: Too open to sleep! Lie down under a spruce's branches.
text.sheltered: You're resting under the spruce, out of the wind.
text.hungry: You're hungry. Look for young birches and willows to browse.
text.no_food: Nothing to eat here. Look for young birches and willows.
text.rain_start: It's starting to rain. Your thick coat keeps you warm.
text.about_looks: The biggest deer in the world: taller than a grown-up at the shoulder, with long pale legs and a droopy nose. Bulls have wide, flat antlers.
text.about_food: Leaves and twigs from birches, willows and aspens, and water plants in summer. In winter, pine twigs.
text.about_home: Lives in forests and bogs. It rests under thick spruces and builds no home at all.
text.about_winter: Stays all winter. Its long legs walk through deep snow, and it eats twigs and pine shoots.
text.about_young: One or two calves are born in early summer. They stay with their mother for a whole year.
text.about_fact: A bull grows new antlers every spring and drops them in winter. Moose are great swimmers.
